segments.text: We have Kerala BJP Chief, MLA from Neemam, former Union Minister of State of Electronics, IT and Skill Development, a technocrat who has now become a full-time politician, an entrepreneur who has now become a full-time politician, who has now shifted base from Delhi to Tiruvananthapuram.
How has it been like, sir?
First of all, thank you for having me and minor correction, I don't know
Why you think I'm a full-time politician only now?
I've been in politics for 20 years.
I'm a three-term MP.
So I think I've been doing full-time politics for about 20 years.
It is true that about two years ago the Prime Minister decided that I should be focused in Kerala.
certainly been in very interesting two years, especially being that all of us, most people outside of Kerala fed this Kerala model, you know, God's own country, story for so many years.
But when you come here and actually understand the reality of what the last 15, 20 years have done to Kerala, I can certainly tell you there's a lot of work to be done.
We had Chief Minister V. D. Satishan earlier today and he said that this is 1991 Dr. Manmohan Singh moment for Kerala where Kerala is entering a new era and breaking away from past.
No, I think he is right on a few counts because this election, 2026 election, was certainly an election where people were angry.
They wanted change.
So that he is right on that account that people want change.
They want a break from the past.
He is also right that Kerala's economy is facing very, very similar challenges that India faced in 1991.
But I would add that India faced similar challenges in 2014 after 10 years of Manmohan Singh.
So I'm not so sure that that analogy is a very accurate analogy to use because he has tremendous headwinds against him.
This is not an easy problem to solve because of all the fiscal problems that the 10 years of CPM have left behind.
And while the story of 1991 India was a story where
liberalization happened and the economy was opened up and investments flowed in, I would respectfully submit that solutions in Kerala are not going to be that simple at all.
It is not going to be easy walk.
This is a tightrope walking that he as a government and his government has to do.
particularly because Kerala is in a major debt trap.

There is very little fiscal headroom for investment and growth and the environment around Kerala, unfortunately he's inherited it but part of it is his making because the Congress has been in government for several years.
the lack of infrastructure, the emigration of talent, the lack of investments and jobs, the high inflation and as we've recently seen the electricity cuts and so on.
So those don't paint a very good picture for investors who have to be a player in the Kerala economy for Kerala's economy to grow.
So he certainly seems to be a man on a mission.
He has presented a white paper, has come up with a roadmap, speaks about Mission Samudra, speaks about other plans that he has for the state.
Would you say that he is more sincere than his predecessor, according to you?
Certainly, I think his predecessor is no standard to be compared to at all.
The 10 years under Pindraya Vijayan, when he started his mandate, he got his mandate in 2016 by saying in Malayalam, that means everything will become alright.
The 10 years on under Pindarai Vijayan, it has certainly been the last decade for Kerala.
The economic situation, the joblessness situation, the highest inflation in the country.
And you are seeing today corruption, institutionalized corruption.
Have you ever heard of DGP of the police force?
being sent to jail for four years for corruption.
And I always wondered when people said about Kerala model and when I was not in Kerala politics, I used to be in awe of that statement.
And it is when you come here that you realize that it was not a Kerala model, it was a CPM model.
and that model was a very, very dysfunctional model.
There was political corruption, there was no development, there was joblessness, there was zero investment, there was zero economic activity, and you were essentially quadrupling debt per capita.
So the 10 years that were before VD Sadesan are certainly no comparison for him.
Anybody will come out looking rosy if you compare them to the 10 years.
But he is certainly a man who has some clear thoughts and I've said this in the assembly.
The white paper was an extremely important move by the government because the people of Kerala now realize the situation that they're in.
And I think, look, good luck to him.
I wish the best for our state.
I wish the best for our people.
And if he can pull it off, more power to him.
But I suspect it's not going to be that simple.
Since you spoke about the assembly and the role of the BJP in the assembly, you have three MLAs including yourself.
The ruling party has 102.
What appears right now is that it is the BJP which is fighting the left more than the current government.
I think that is each one.

I mean, it's a funny situation where the Congress will claim that we have an understanding with the left before the election and then the left will claim that we have an understanding with the Congress.
Somehow that makes us feel very important.
If both of them are claiming that the other is their friend, it seems to me that the case is being made that we are very relevant.
to their politics.
But are you?
You have been trying very hard for several years now to get some kind of toe hold in the state and that is really not happening.
No Maria look let's be let's be objective and clear.
Who's in an alliance with whom nationally?
I just have to point out to you there is a thing called Indy Alliance.
It's supposed to be a political formation where they sit and have chai and coffee in Delhi regularly.
Each of them take turns in calling the BJP fascists.
They are both the CPM of the Congress.
They are in cahoots, they are in a political alliance, in a formal political alliance in every state in this country.
in every election in this country from Tripura to Rajasthan to Tamil Nadu.
The CPM and Congress are in a formal alliance and they want to pull a fast one here and pretend that they are not.
Look, I will trot out chapter and verse about how they are still in cahoots.
The Shabarimala loot scam.
It was an electoral issue four months on
Four and a half months on, the Congress government has done zero to put the CPM ministers behind bars.
The ExaLogic, where a sitting Chief Minister's daughter has been accused of corruption, it is a case to be filed under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
The sitting Chief Minister, the Congress Chief Minister, who basically got the mandate, arguing that Pindray vision was corrupt, has not made a move on it yet.
So look, these are games that politicians play.
We all understand that.
We're all grown-up people.
We understand the games that politicians play.
But I think the era of making fools of Malayalis and playing this game of you once, then me once, and you once, and me once, and making BJP the common target,
by calling us communal.
That chapter is over.
That game is over.
People now see development and opportunity as the main issue, and they're asking which party can deliver.
prosperity which party can deliver development and it is that party that they will support.

Yes, so you speak about prosperity but why is it that the BJP is not able to convince the people of Kerala because you have tried really hard for several years now and particularly since 2014 when we speak about the new BJP there has been lot of emphasis on Kerala.
No, there is a simple answer for that and it is obviously dated, predated my arrival
The narrative about BJP that has been successfully manufactured in Kerala for not just one day or one month, for several decades is that BJP is a Hindu party.
BJP is a communal party.
That the BJP is against Christians and against Muslims.
And that stuck.
And maybe part of it was our fault, we did not contest it enough.
Maybe our silence led people to believe that that is true.
But it is the furthest thing from the truth.

And today, we have a situation that the people who call the BJP communal, the same government have ministers from the Indian Union Muslim League, a party to whom Rahul Gandhi gave a certificate saying it's a secular party, saying, madhamana, madhamana, madhamadi.
They're saying it openly, because religion is our issue, religion is our issue, religion issue.
And you have the temerity to call us communal.
Look, the history of Kerala politics is that BJP has been put into a corner by both these parties.
And you're not able to corner it or counter it?
No, no, of course we have countered it.
If you have got fifteen, fourteen and a half percent, fifteen percent vote, thirty lakh people have voted for us in this election.
Three MLAs have won the election.
We have got Tiruvindram corporation, two municipalities and a score of panchayats where BJP is governing.
And in the NDA coalition today, there are Christian parties that are in the NDA coalition.
So I think, look, this is the beginning of a significant change in Kerala politics.
The old model is just not going to work it anymore.
That is why today you have, and I'm happy, by the way, when V.D.
Sathishan or the Chief Minister of Kerala is now talking development.
He's talking about Project Samudra.
He's talking about port-led development.
I'm extremely happy.
that for the first time center stage
The main topic of discourse is the future of Kerala.
I'm glad you came here and you're talking about the future of Kerala.
And the future of Kerala is not some trashy discussion on communalism and secularism, some fake discourse on that.
It is about are people getting the development that they deserve?
Should children be the talent of our state, be exported out of the state and go and work and find jobs and study elsewhere around the world?
Talent is the biggest asset that we have in our state, and today, the average age of our state is going up because all the youngsters are leaving our state.
Those are issues to be discussed, not these fake 20-year-old, 30-year-old narrative about who is more secular and who is less secular.

You know, since you speak about the state having the required talent pool but is not able to really cash on it because most of them have left the state or migrated out of it because of perhaps lack of opportunities, their aspirations were not aligned with the state's growth story.
Now, here is the Chief Minister who is saying that he is trying to
write a different chapter altogether and that's where I want to understand from you.
Do you think at this point that is really possible particularly given the competition that you have coming in from neighboring states?
No, like I said before to you Maria, we wish you well.
We want our state to do well.
We want our children to get jobs.
We want the education system in Kerala to be modernized.
We want our colleges to be top class.
We want our farmers to be commercially viable.
All of these things, if any government does, we will fully support them.
I said this in the assembly.
But the problem with this is when you dish out these promises and paint a dream,
build a dream, you should also do some due diligence on whether you're able to do it.

If 150 days on, a government that promised five guarantees is unable to fulfill four out of the five guarantees, 120 days on, the only thing that has gone up is the per capita debt and the gross debt of the state government.
Not one job, not one investment, not one company to come in here.
If 120 days on, you have power cuts,
and you blame the rain for the power cuts.
Now if that starts then every state government of BJP should blame the rains for the power cuts.
What will you do in Delhi?
You will go line up in front of the power minister.
My issue is not whether his dream is a compelling dream, whether his vision is a compelling vision, whether what he wants to do is sincere or not.
But I will argue today to you and I say with full responsibility, he will come up a cropper, he will not be able to deliver.
because of what he has inherited and the very little wiggle room he has and be, most importantly, the political stand that he is being forced to take that he will not cooperate with the center.
There is no state in this country that can do well if you are at loggerheads with the center.
This is just common sensical… No, but he is saying that he will cooperate with the center.
But he is not.
That is for the state's good.
No, no.
I am saying… I can say many things including the fact that I want to be president of the US.
But that's not… that's not what I say.
It's what I do that is important.
He is against PM Sri.
How will you reform the educational system in Kerala?
If you say, I will not implement PM Sri.
How will you…
give better opportunities to poor children for better school.
If the Muslim League Education Minister says we should throw PM Sri into the Arabian Sea.
If you want cooperation and support from the government of India, you have to create the conducive atmosphere for it.
You can't expect, ek taali se haath nahi bastaa.
To quote in Kerala, I should not be speaking Hindi.
You have to have a relationship with the centre where you place the interests of the people of Kerala primarily and then play politics later on.
You play politics during election time based on your performance.
120 days later, tell me where we are on the education system in Kerala.
Do we have any visibility of what he is going to do?
No, he doesn't have it either.
So these are harsh realities.
It is all okay to be a politician today, make a lot of reels, make a lot of great… So he makes reels, is that what you're saying?
I mean the Congress politics is now reduced to that.
You make a lot of reels of people having tea, coffee… Rahul Gandhi?
So since you're talking about Rahul Gandhi, let's talk about what he is saying, UPI tax.
You were in Metis, and you had projected UPI as for something which is common good or good for the people.
And here is MDR which is coming in.
The Congress and the critics of that are saying that this is some kind of surrender to the US pressure because the MasterCard and visa,
these are two US companies which lost out because of the sheer spread of the UPI.
And now you are trying to give that UPI in itself some kind of setback.
Maria, I always wonder what is the best way to characterize Rahul Gandhi.
I always lose to describe him, to find a way to describe him.
But I've come to one conclusion.
He's certainly a brand ambassador for a headache tablet.
Because what he does really gives everybody's common sensible man a headache.
Because you are wondering what is he saying?
UPI today is a globally accepted, globally respected, globally fated platform of financial transactions and digital money and digital financial transactions.
It is the biggest ecosystem in the world.
Yes, and many countries are adopting it because it is cost, it's very inexpensive, it is smooth, it's efficient.
Now, the government and the players, including the NPCI and the RBI have decided to add a nominal charge for a transaction between an individual and a merchant.
Merchants are an ecosystem that understand very clearly the concept of an MDR.
MDR, they charge for credit cards, they charge for debit cards, they charge for... What is Rahul Gandhi's problem with this?
I don't understand.
Is he out of pocket on these transactions?
Is he worried that his monthly bill is going to... He's not saying what his problem is, but this manufactured controversy that this is a tax.
How is it a tax?
What is it a tax?
The MDR means what?
Merchant transaction rate, merchant discount rate.
What is that?
I'm yet to understand, despite all the posts and the rhetoric from the Congress, what is the point that they're making?
That something that is free should remain free forever.
Is that the point?
Then why don't we just argue that passenger train tickets should be free?
Why don't we argue that every service should be free?
If it is free, somebody else is paying the bill for it.
This is a transaction between an individual and a merchant.
And the merchant is being charged a particular fee for it.
Full stop.
He's demanding a rollback.
No, no, he can demand what he can, he can demand whatever he wants, that's okay.
He's sitting in an echo chamber where there are three people giving him thalis every time he says something silly and stupid.
But we don't have to listen to that.
My point is if he's saying something sensible, we are all here to respond to it or argue with it or have a discourse.
But what is remotely sensible about what he's saying?
You are essentially saying that this is some kind of misinformation campaign.
It is not misinformation campaign.
It is just complete, plain, manufactured controversy.

You create a controversy out of nothing, and you act very completely outraged by it, hope that somebody picks it up and gets similarly outraged by it, and hopefully that will cost it into multiple people getting outraged.
But if you just slice and dice it and understand, put it under a microscope and understand what the issue is, UPI today is an extremely successful ecosystem, platform, number one, tick mark.
Many, many people in the country are completely using UPR.
I'm benefited by it.
No peer-to-peer transaction is being charged, tick mark.
Who is being charged?
A merchant is being charged.
A merchant as in a commercial enterprise is being charged a nominal charge for using the UPI.
That money will be used to invest in UPI.
That money will be used to modernize UPI.
And it also gives the merchant a sense of responsibility that it's a paid service.
This is all very reasonable, logical decision making on part of a government that is reasonable, logical and will never sacrifice consumer interest at any, at the annual of anything.
But when it was conceptualized, it was free for all.
Look, here's the thing.
When you have something and it is still free for all,
That's the point I'm making.
It was conceptualized to be a very smooth, frictionless, inexpensive way of transacting digitally.
And that design element is intact.
The only change now is that the merchant side of it is being asked to pay a nominal fee.
The consumer at large is unaffected.
And the design feature that the UPI consumer will get frictionless, cheap, inexpensive, easy to use digital payment platform is completely unchanged.
So that cap of 2000 rupees, that above 2000 there will be an MDR of 0.4%?
Correct.
And that is for the merchants to pay?
Yes.
So, this entire controversy, would you say that this is much ado about nothing?
It is not only much ado about nothing, it is much ado about minus nothing.
I mean, I don't even understand where the ado comes from.
I mean, much ado implies that there is some ado.
What is the ado?
If somebody can explain to me, I'm a reasonably intelligent man.
I was a minister there for three and a half years.
I understand the UPI ecosystem reasonably well.
I don't claim to be a genius like Raoul Gandhi.
I don't read any fat books like him, but I certainly have a highly developed common sense.
What is the issue somebody tells me I can argue?
It is like P. Chidambaram saying that this is a surrender to the US pressure quote unquote Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party.
Look, I can't answer this stuff because this is all conspiracy theories that make Oliver Stone look like an amateur.
These are all made up where who makes it up.
He probably has a department just manufactures these things as he goes along.
The foreign ministry issued a press note about the 100% tariff in clear, stark terms saying we will never sacrifice our nation's interest.
And that comes first, second, third, fourth and fifth.
Do you see any Indian buying this argument that Prime Minister Narendra Modi Ji will surrender to Visa and MasterCard because Rahul Gandhi wants him to?
So let's move away from that and talk about the one-day Mataram controversy.
I'm sitting in a state which is ruled by Congress Party.
The Chief Minister says that in this state there will be only two stanzas, something that the Congress Working Committee has approved of.
But here is a law of the land which says clearly that it has to be about all the stanzas.
What does BJP stand in the state of Kerala?
BJP stand in the state of Kerala means that BJP stand all over.
What is the law of the land is the law of the land.
When the parliament passes a law, it is not subject to the congress here or the Muslim League in the north of Kerala to determine
what parts of the law they will follow or not.
I mean, I think they are living in fool's paradise and in, you know, lala land, if they think they can chop and dice the constitution.
These are the same people who hold the constitution up every time they take an oath in parliament.
This is the same Rahul Gandhi who goes around the world saying the constitution democracy is under a challenge and threat.
No, I have said this publicly in my press conference.
These people are living in La La Land.
If they think that today, the national song, they will not sing four stanzas, which means what?
Tomorrow, the national anthem, they can say, because Kerala is not mentioned in this dravid, we will not sing the national anthem.
And this is all cuckoo.
This is pandering to the lowest common denominator of politics.
The Chief Minister, if he has any common sense, he took an oath saying, uphold the law, I will uphold the Constitution.
He should have a common sense to understand.
This is not things to be playing football with.
You are part of a constitutional democracy.
You are a state.
You're not some adjunct of the Middle East or something.
However much the Indian Union Muslim League likes to believe that, you have to follow the laws of the land, otherwise the consequences is something that you'll have to deal with.
So he's following what the Congress party has agreed on?
Well, that's what I'm saying.
If the Congress party believes that they can create a system within a system, and that system within a system is ruled by some crown prince and some crown princes,
and their friends in the Muslim League.
If they believe that, then it is, they are, like I said, they're living a delusional, fictional land.
My last question and this is to Kerala BJP chief.

Do you have a clear roadmap since you say that right now what you started five years ago in your ministry is being implemented and it has its fifth year, is there some madman idea also for the BJP in the state?
No madman idea at all.
I have a very clear, lucid idea, which is that it is clear that the people of Kerala have begun to understand that the CPM and the Congress are the two sides of one coin called Indy.
And really, the alternate political formation is the BJP-India.
And this is the proposition that we are putting forth in front of them, leading up to 29 Lok Sabha elections.
Mr. Rajiv Chandrasekhar, always a pleasure speaking to you.
Thank you for so much of honesty.
Thank you so much.
